task.task_name: Triage a software customer support ticket
task.task_description: You work in customer support at a B2B software company. A customer reports that several employees can't access their reporting dashboard after a recent software update. They've included a short description, screenshots, and roughly when the problem started. You can look up their account information, previous support tickets, product documentation, and known incidents. Your job is to figure out what kind of issue this is, how serious it might be, and how it's affecting the customer's business. Some tickets are straightforward, while others may involve widespread outages, unclear symptoms, or problems that need specialist attention. Decide who should handle the issue, make sure the ticket gets to the right team with the relevant information, and let the customer know what happens next. You're responsible for triaging the ticket, not troubleshooting or resolving the underlying problem.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Review the reported symptoms and evidence
operational_subtasks.description: Read the ticket description and review its screenshots and reported timing to identify the observed behavior and information already provided.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one routine review per ticket; allow a few minutes to compare the short description with the supplied images and onset information. This is the initial evidence review, not a technical investigation.

operational_subtasks.description: Check the customer account and previous support tickets for relevant context about the affected users, service, and similar prior reports.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one account-and-history lookup per ticket, taking about 4 minutes when records are available. This gathers customer context once for use in later assessments; it does not repeat review of the current report.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Check product guidance and known incidents
operational_subtasks.description: Compare the reported behavior and timing with relevant product documentation and known incident information.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one targeted search per ticket, averaging about 6 minutes across routine cases; an evident match may take less, while a limited search takes longer. This is evidence gathering, not troubleshooting.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Seek clarification when material details are missing
operational_subtasks.description: When the available evidence leaves a material uncertainty about symptoms or affected scope, ask the customer a focused question and assess any reply received during triage.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Model assumption: this is needed for about 1 in 5 tickets, with roughly 5 minutes of active effort per occurrence to identify the gap, contact the customer, and use any timely reply; waiting is excluded. Routine cases require no clarification.

operational_subtasks.description: Use the reported and gathered evidence to determine the likely issue type, such as an access issue, product problem, or known incident, and note material uncertainty.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one classification decision per ticket, averaging about 3 minutes of incremental analysis using findings already gathered. Do not repeat the underlying record or product-information review.

operational_subtasks.description: Assess the apparent scope and business effect of the issue, including the number of affected employees and any relevant account context or known incident information.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one impact assessment per ticket, averaging about 4 minutes to weigh existing evidence and determine apparent seriousness. This is an additional assessment, not a second evidence-gathering pass.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Select the handling team and route the ticket
operational_subtasks.description: Choose the appropriate team or specialist based on the issue category and seriousness, then route the ticket with a concise summary of the symptoms, impact, relevant evidence, and unresolved uncertainty.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one routing and handoff per ticket, averaging about 3 minutes using the findings already available. This covers selecting the recipient and entering or transferring relevant information, not downstream investigation or resolution.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Tell the customer what happens next
operational_subtasks.description: Send the customer a concise update describing the triage disposition, the team handling the ticket, and the next expected step without representing that the underlying problem has been resolved.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one customer update per ticket, averaging about 2 minutes to prepare and send using the routing decision and existing findings. Any separate wait for a reply is excluded.

parent_output_contract.completion_boundary: The ticket's issue category and apparent seriousness and business impact have been assessed, the ticket has been routed to the selected handling team with relevant information, and the customer has been told what happens next.
scope_exclusions: Troubleshooting or resolving the underlying software problem
The receiving team's investigation or specialist work
Subsequent approvals, remediation, or customer follow-up beyond the triage update

activities.activity_name: Review and validate the agent's triage disposition
activities.description: Review the agent's evidence summary, issue category, impact assessment, routing, and customer update as one connected triage disposition. Assess whether the conclusions and communication are supported by the reported information, account context, and cited product or incident evidence; pay particular attention to material uncertainty or conflicting evidence. Correct or follow up on material errors before relying on the disposition. This review supports the support agent's ownership of the customer response and does not require formal approval or repeat the agent's research.
activities.trigger: For each triaged ticket, when the agent has produced its findings, routing, and customer update and those outputs are to be accepted as completing triage.
activities.expected_action: Evaluate the agent's outputs for consistency, evidential support, appropriate handling-team selection, and accurate next-step messaging; correct or request revision when material issues are found.
